bull.b: A predominantly recurring revenue base supports visibility, customer lifetime value and scalable economics. Usage-based subscription expansion can also increase revenue as customers send more messages, reach more users and adopt additional capabilities.

Strong retention, expansion and growth among large customers indicate durable product value and increasing enterprise penetration. Larger account adoption can support multiyear revenue growth and improve operating leverage as the platform scales.

bull.t: Improving Cash Generation and Low Leverage
bull.b: Positive free cash flow despite GAAP losses demonstrates improving cash conversion and financial discipline. Low leverage preserves flexibility to fund product investment, support enterprise growth and absorb execution challenges without significant balance-sheet strain.

bear.t: GAAP Losses and Slowing Revenue Growth
bear.b: The company has not yet demonstrated sustainable GAAP earnings power, and historical growth has decelerated materially. Continued investment and slower expansion could delay durable profitability and make results more dependent on successful execution of the growth plan.

bear.t: Gross Margin Pressure from Messaging Costs
bear.b: Premium messaging and carrier costs can structurally pressure software margins as channel usage increases, even when fees are passed to customers. Additional delivery staffing for AI products may further limit margin expansion until scale and pricing offset these costs.

Fast expansion of engineering and sales capacity raises ramp, coordination and spending risks during an important product rollout. A CFO transition adds leadership continuity risk while Braze is balancing growth investment, margin management and its path to profitability.
